counterfactual_missing_items: homogeneous fat signal on T1 and T2 (expected for lipoma)
dense sclerotic bone without diploic involvement (expected for osteoma)
decisive_items: well-defined, 19-mm mass in the left parietal bone near the squamosal suture, centred in the diploic space, with sparse but preserved trabeculae and a slight bony bulge
The hyperintense foci on T1 images were presumed to represent bone marrow fat
response.rationale: R2 best matches the imaging features: a well-defined diploic mass with preserved trabeculae, T1 hyperintense foci (fat), heterogeneous T2, and restricted diffusion, classic for hemangioma. C1 is a redundant completion of R2, adding no new diagnostic information. R1 (lipoma) is contradicted by restricted diffusion and heterogeneous T2; R5 (osteoma) is contradicted by the diploic location and preserved trabeculae.

rejected.why: Lipoma would show homogeneous fat signal on MRI and lack restricted diffusion; the lesion's heterogeneous T2 and restricted diffusion are inconsistent.
Osteoma typically appears as a dense sclerotic mass without diploic involvement or preserved trabeculae; the described features point away from osteoma.
